_comment: Reasoned statuses for failure-matrix cases that cannot be executed as live or automated tests yet. Used by scripts/matrix-coverage.py only when no test/lab evidence exists, or, for an entry with 'requires' (evidence kinds such as native_e2e), until evidence of one of those kinds exists; the reason is shown as the case's note either way. 'blocked', 'partial' and 'not_applicable' are never counted as passed; 'verified_check' records an executed check script (exact command, artifacts and result) that CI re-runs on every release artifact. An entry with "pinned": true is never promoted by discovered tests or lab passes that name the case (its evidence is elsewhere, such as a hosted workflow run); only editing the entry changes that. A failing lab result still shows as failing_live.

TRUST-012.reason: Anvil does not ingest or correlate gateway logs; it never confirms anything from temporal proximity. Operator logs are used only as lab ground truth.

LOAD-012.reason: The optional JMeter adapter is not built in this release (plan 14.3: only after native load works). Native load covers the required workloads; see docs/load.md.

PROTO-004.reason: HTTP/2 GOAWAY and REFUSED_STREAM are typed (exchange.h2_goaway / exchange.h2_refused_stream, dispatch derived from REFUSED_STREAM) but a live multi-stream graceful-shutdown fixture is not built yet.

REL-001.reason: Hosted release smoke (.github/workflows/release-smoke.yml) against the published, unsigned anvil-v0.1.5 assets (each checked against SHA256SUMS): run 41275148483 on PR head 70dde1b2, with the same per-target result as the earlier runs 41273823587 (head f00000e6), 41270507104 (head 4d707c55), 41255989645 (head 8edbdfa8), 41254710916 (head 51fbc0b8), 41189324002 (head adb4d3f) and 41185287833 (head 7f17212). This evidence comes from pull_request-triggered runs against the published assets; once the workflow is on main, the run that publishing a release starts (release: published) is the routine check. For each target, the smoke installs the package natively on a fresh runner and launches the installed app (window observed, and a webview content process attributed to the app: on Linux by process tree, on macOS by launchctl's responsible pid, on Windows as a WebView2 descendant). It then imports samples/workspaces/anvil-samples.anvil, sends its Healthy/OK request to a loopback listener (HTTP 200) and relaunches the app; a target stops at its first failed step. Six targets pass every step: macOS arm64 DMG (macos-15), macOS x86_64 DMG (native Intel macos-15-intel), Windows x64 NSIS and MSI (windows-2025), Linux x64 .deb (Ubuntu 26.04) and .rpm (Fedora 44). The x64 AppImage fails at its first launch (a package failure): the app starts and shows its window, but its WebKit web process aborts with EGL_BAD_PARAMETER, so it never reached the import, the call or the relaunch. The fix, ferrum-edge/ferrum-anvil#463, is merged but not released: 0.1.5's AppImage stays broken until the next release ships a rebuilt one. The GUI was not driven: the import and the call go through the release CLI archive on the app's data directory. Recorded bypasses: Gatekeeper and SmartScreen were never consulted (the assets carried no quarantine attribute or Mark-of-the-Web); the DMG license was accepted non-interactively; the installers ran silently, the MSI as an administrator without a UAC prompt; local .deb/.rpm packages and the AppImage ran without a package-signature check. Still blocked: signed and notarized first-run acceptance on macOS and Windows (Gatekeeper, SmartScreen, Keychain), which needs owner credentials (ferrum-edge/ferrum-anvil#2). Linux has no platform code signing, so it waits on no credentials.

REL-003.reason: Refusal is automated against built bundles: .github/workflows/updater-e2e.yml builds the e2e-instrumented desktop bundle (AppImage on ubuntu-26.04, .app on macos-15) with a minisign key generated for the run and a loopback update endpoint (requireSignedVersion stays on), and drives the app's update_install command through WebDriver (apps/desktop/e2e/updater/). An update signed by another key, one with a corrupted signature and one altered after signing are each refused with the plugin's minisign error after the app requested the manifest and the artifact; during each refusal the bundle's files (SHA-256, mode, size, inode, mtime), the reported version and the persistent profile files (SQLite's -shm read index excluded) are unchanged. Relaunched afterwards, the bundle matches its recorded contents and reports its own version, and the same profile unlocks with the same workspaces; a validly signed update installs and the relaunched bundle reports the new version. The rel_003_* unit tests run more signature variants through the same updater path on Tauri's mock runtime. Not covered: Windows (MSI/NSIS), release-profile bundles without the e2e feature, TLS and the published latest.json, .deb/.rpm (no in-app update). The valid path was also run by hand on macOS arm64 from 0.1.0 to 0.1.1 (release runs 36827029766 and 36835226571, updater key BFE08514FEC0E65A); macOS may re-prompt for Keychain access after an update of an unsigned build (ferrum-edge/ferrum-anvil#2).

REL-006.reason: Executed check: .github/workflows/website-evidence.yml checks out ferrum-edge/ferrumedge at the pinned commit e4fe8b9a1b1de6b8dfeb021111bea262828fe57c (main after ferrum-edge/ferrumedge#105), verifies HEAD is that commit, runs the website's own tests (`node --test --test-reporter=tap "tests/**/*.test.js"`, Node 22.23.3, RUN_LIVE_ASSET_CHECKS unset) and uploads website-evidence.json (website SHA, command, counts, exit code, result). release.yml calls it on every release run (tag push or dry run), beside the build; a failure shows in the run but does not gate the draft release. It also runs on manual dispatch and on changes to the workflow. Hosted runs pass 403 of 405 tests with 0 failed and 2 skipped (the two live highlight.js CDN checks in tests/components.test.js, unrelated to Anvil): workflow_dispatch run 41280626152 on main f2beb1b8 (2026-11-01); push run 41185707622 and workflow_dispatch run 41185714154 on main 21d8778; and, through release.yml, the website job of release dry runs 41234488118 and 41192909519. The check covers the website at the pinned commit, which describes anvil-v0.1.5; a later release's pages are covered once the pin moves to a website commit that describes it. Tests (tests/anvil.test.js, 'Anvil downloads match the release evidence'): each download.html row's OS and architecture, and each link's package label and column, match the linked asset name (architecture aliases mapped; a swapped architecture, OS, package or column is rejected by a negative test); every displayed download is that platform's installer or CLI archive in the recorded release-evidence.json, and the table shows each of them once; the recorded SHA256SUMS lines hash to GitHub's digest of the published SHA256SUMS asset, each of the 33 listed assets has a recorded digest equal to its SHA256SUMS entry (only SHA256SUMS and release-evidence.json are unlisted), and every displayed download is checksummed there. 'published preview links and bounded claims' requires every release-download link in Anvil content to be a published asset of the audited tag, so no asset name is inferred from the tag; tests/releases.test.js requires download.html to link SHA256SUMS and release-evidence.json. The site displays no hashes and points to SHA256SUMS. Scope: asset names and digests are compared as recorded in tests/fixtures/release-audit.json (GitHub release API, checked 2026-10-31), not re-fetched on each run; the release API returned the same 35 asset names and digests on 2026-11-01.

Tests: tests/components.test.js 'Anvil navigation entries' runs the site's components.js, with its real DOMContentLoaded handler, for root (/, /index.html), extensionless and .html (/anvil, /anvil.html, /foundry), guide (/guides/, /guides/anvil-getting-started, /guides/anvil-diagnostics.html) and other nested (/install/linux, /plugins/) page paths: the desktop Tools dropdown, the mobile menu and the footer each carry one Anvil link labelled unsigned preview, written with ./ or ../ as the page's depth requires and resolving to /anvil, and the footer's Anvil guides link resolves to /guides/#anvil-guides; on /anvil and /anvil.html Tools is the only active section and the desktop and mobile Anvil links carry aria-current="page"; an Anvil guide activates Docs and marks no Anvil link current; another Tools page does not mark Anvil current; no injected link uses .html. 'normalizePath' and 'resolveActiveNav' cover the same paths with and without .html, index and trailing slashes; 'the injected nav and banner use data hooks the listener handles' requires aria-controls on every dropdown toggle. tests/anvil.test.js checks that every local link in Anvil content (the six Anvil pages and the Anvil blocks on download, guides/index, index and releases) is extensionless and resolves from its own page, with its anchor; that the anchors other pages link to and the anvil.html jump links exist; and that Anvil screenshots and brand images carry alt text. Scope: the shell is rendered in a Node vm with a minimal DOM, not a browser or a mobile viewport (the mobile menu is checked as markup); accessibility is the targeted aria-current, aria-controls and alt-text checks, not a full audit. No test asserts that a page mounts the shared nav; at the pinned commit all ten of those pages carry nav-container and footer-container and load components.js at their depth.

REL-008.reason: Partial: the hosted check runs and passes (.github/workflows/website-evidence.yml, called from release.yml on every release run: the website's tests at ferrum-edge/ferrumedge commit e4fe8b9a1b1de6b8dfeb021111bea262828fe57c, 403 of 405 passed with 0 failed and 2 unrelated live CDN checks skipped, in workflow_dispatch run 41280626152 on main f2beb1b8, runs 41185707622 and 41185714154 on main 21d8778, and release dry runs 41234488118 and 41192909519), but those tests check a named subset of the site's claims, not that it advertises only built and tested capabilities. Covered by tests/anvil.test.js: no Anvil content claims an exact or guaranteed root cause, 'available now', 'now available' or 'download now'; every Anvil page and block carries the unsigned-preview notice naming v0.1.5; downloads distinguish installer code signing from updater signatures; compatibility and limitations name the eight catalog releases and the ferrum.catalog.unavailable fallback; the support matrix lists gRPC over HTTP/3, gRPC-Web, SSE over HTTP/3, CONNECT-UDP, PROXY protocol, HBONE and 0-RTT early data, gives WebSocket, gRPC, gRPC-Web, SSE, TCP and UDP/DTLS a load unit, and its 'Not implemented' note lists the remaining gaps and no implemented protocol; the JWT-SVID and TLS auth rows, the load-tests guide's units and refusals and the auth guide's Workload API section are pinned; stale single-release, HTTP-only load and 11-profile lab claims are rejected; Anvil screenshots sit in figures captioned 'Pre-release build' with descriptive alt text. Missing: the expected values are written into the tests, not compared with an Anvil capability or test manifest, and several advertised claims have no test: the Capabilities and Workflows sections of anvil.html (OpenAPI 2.0-3.2, WSDL 1.1, Postman, Insomnia, cURL and HAR import; the collection runner with datasets and JUnit, HTML or JSON reports; HDR percentiles and HTML, JSON or CSV load reports; encryption at rest and profile locking), the API key, Basic/Bearer, JWT signing, OAuth 2.0, Ferrum HMAC v2, DPoP, WS-Security and multi-auth rows, the support-matrix cells beyond those above, and the per-release catalog outcome counts (556 for 0.9.15 down to 528 for 0.9.5). Screenshot content is not compared with the current app. Settled when website tests tie each advertised capability to Anvil's built and tested capabilities (for example a capability manifest published by Anvil) and the pin moves to that website commit.

UP-017.reason: Live reproduction blocked: Ferrum Edge 0.9.5 assigns port_exhaustion only to EADDRNOTAVAIL at connect (src/retry.rs) and the release binary has no lab dial-admission hook, while draining the lab host's real ephemeral ports would be unsafe. Covered instead by the public-signal contract test up_017_port_exhaustion_signal_is_coarse_and_hook_free (crates/anvil-diagnostics/tests/upstream_setup_contract.rs): the catalog's shared 502 connection_failure 'Backend unavailable' signal keeps the connection-failure family ambiguous, names port exhaustion only as an unknown-confidence candidate, never states port exhaustion or host resources at likely or above, and makes no TLS/DNS claim. It is neither a live nor a hook-based test.

UP-019.reason: Live reproduction blocked: upstream.trust_withdrawn is mesh-only in 0.9.5 and 0.9.7 (an accepted gateway trust publication withdraws an authority while an HBONE / sidecar-mTLS transport is established or reused). The mesh lab profile runs HBONE with SPIFFE identities and reproduces the unauthenticated-peer refusal, but it has no control plane publishing trust, so no withdrawal on a live tunnel is reproduced. Covered instead by the public-signal contract test up_019_trust_withdrawn_signal_makes_no_certificate_claim (crates/anvil-diagnostics/tests/upstream_setup_contract.rs): the shared 502 connection_failure signal stays ambiguous, lists trust withdrawal only as an unknown-confidence candidate, and yields no confirmed or likely certificate/TLS claim and no blame on the caller's certificate.
